business_problem: Catalyst Brands needed to speed up product and creative cycles across a portfolio of retail brands, because traditional design, asset iteration, and analysis workflows were too slow and expensive for a market that moves at digital speed.
solution_summary: Catalyst Brands uses Gemini Enterprise as the AI foundation for product design, merchandising, analysis, and internal prototyping across brands including JCPenney, Aéropostale, Brooks Brothers, Lucky Brand, and Nautica. Teams use Gemini to brainstorm and rapidly prototype new concepts, while visual models such as Veo help transform still images and sketches into dynamic videos that can be iterated without organizing additional creative shoots. NotebookLM and Deep Research give business teams faster ways to analyze complex information and ground product ideas in real data, and code-generation tooling lowers the barrier for non-experts to create working software or UI concepts. This architecture turns AI into a shared workflow layer rather than a niche experiment, helping Catalyst move from idea to market faster while also building the internal confidence and culture needed for a broader retail AI transformation.

data_flow: Creative and merchandising teams start with product or campaign ideas, use Gemini and visual models to generate and iterate concepts, enrich those concepts with NotebookLM and Deep Research, and then move promising outputs into code or production workflows with coding agents and enterprise AI support.
business_outcome: Catalyst Brands reduced time to market, accelerated creative prototyping, enabled non-engineers to produce working code, and created a shared AI operating model that helps its retail teams respond faster to fashion demand.
